subject: Request: Gradual launch + auto-revert guard for AtlasPay integration
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@atlaspay.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prod launch plan & SLA ask for Redwood integration

Hi Ben,

We’re targeting a staged production launch of AtlasPay’s Redwood integration the week of Jun 21. Procurement flagged that AtlasPay needs an explicit SLA mitigation plan for any rollout that could affect our checkout latency SLA.

Specifically, we want to ensure:
- An automated rollback or pin to a safe model/version if errors spike or latency regresses.
- A canary window and traffic split that limits blast radius.
- A documented fallback (either smaller model or cached responses) with clear triggers.

Attached is our procurement baseline (SLA-req.xlsx). Can you send a proposed rollout policy we can include in the SOW and share what exceptions to Redwood’s standard SLA you’d need (if any)?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Director, Platform Integrations — AtlasPay

Attachment: SLA-req.xlsx (spreadsheet, 74KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Moreno <alex@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@atlaspay.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-05T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch plan & SLA ask for Redwood integration

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to outline a practical guardrail we can ship with the integration. High level: Redwood can support a staged A/B (canary) rollout with automatic revert + pinned fallback. Draft policy attached (proposed-rollout.yaml).

Key points (summary):
- Canary size: start at 5% traffic for 2 hours, then 20% for 4 hours before full cutover.
- Health metrics: p95 latency target <= 300ms, error rate < 0.5% (both measured at service ingress).
- Auto-revert triggers:
  * 5-minute rolling error rate > 1% for 3 consecutive windows, OR
  * p95 latency breach (>300ms) for 3 consecutive 5-min windows, OR
  * significant increase in downstream timeouts (>2x baseline)
- Pinning: if auto-revert fires, traffic will pin to last known-good model version; we can also pin to a quantized/safer variant for up to 48 hours while we investigate.
- Fallback: default to cached responses for deterministic endpoints and to a smaller model variant for free-text paths (configurable per-route).

Operational requirements from AtlasPay:
- Shared uptime/latency telemetry access (read-only) via an SSO link during the canary.
- A mutual action plan (simple checklist) and a primary on-call contact for post-mortem.

I attached the YAML with recommended thresholds and rollout schedule. If that looks OK, we’ll route this for a short exception approval (SLA carve-out) and a DocuSign amendment.

Next steps:
1) Confirm thresholds and canary windows (reply-all).
2) We’ll create the DocuSign amendment and a short MPO (mutual plan of operations).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-rollout.yaml (text)

Subject: Re: Prod launch plan & SLA ask for Redwood integration

Ben — looping in Aditya for SLA carve-out approval and finance for potential credit/term changes. A couple of asks from our side:
- If the canary auto-reverts, we should automatically disable any scheduled traffic ramps until engineering confirms the fix.
- Request a 48-hour notification window before any force-cutover (i.e., an override that pushes 100% traffic).

Alex — can you confirm AtlasPay’s on-call for the go/no-go windows and add them to the MPO? Also, procurement will expect a DocuSign amendment.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch plan & SLA ask for Redwood integration — conditional approval

Marissa / Ben — I reviewed the proposed policy. I’m granting a conditional SLA exception with the following non-negotiables:

1) Auto-revert + pin to last-known-good version must be enforced by the routing policy with a signed off playbook (owned by AtlasPay on-call and Redwood on-call).
2) Canary telemetry (p95, error-rate, timeout count) must be streamed to our ops dashboard and shared read-only with AtlasPay during the window.
3) No automated force-cutover without 48-hour written notice to both sides.
4) Any exception period will include a 1-week reduced SLA credit schedule (to be finalized by finance) and a mandatory 72-hour post-launch review.

Please proceed to generate the DocuSign amendment and the MPO. Once procurement signs, finance and legal will finalize the credit schedule.

I’ve attached a short approval note for records.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

Attachment: approval-note.pdf (PDF, 9KB)
